narrative.title: The Tallest Relay Mast Count
narrative.scenario: A broadcast network diagrams its relay masts as a binary tree, with the studio at the root and each mast feeding at most two downstream masts. Signal-latency budgeting depends on one number: how many masts a packet traverses on the longest root-to-leaf chain. The network planner needs that count for every redesigned topology before signing off on hardware.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an integer: the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.

testCases.explanation: The deepest chain is 3 -> 20 -> 15 (or -> 7): three nodes.
Root plus its single left child spans two nodes.

hintLevels: Level 1: Height is a per-node question — 'how deep does the ground get below me?' — answered bottom-up.
Level 2: An empty subtree contributes 0; a node's height is 1 plus the taller of its two children's heights.
Level 3: The recursion touches every node once, and the call stack depth is the very height you're measuring.
